title: Local functions versus lambdas (named helpers vs inline callbacks)
hook: A local function is a named method nested inside another method. It can use yield return, recurse naturally, and skip delegate allocation when you call it directly — things a lambda cannot do.

blocks.text: A **local function** is a method declared inside another member's body. It has no access modifier and is visible throughout the containing member. Non-static local functions can read enclosing locals and `this`. **static** local functions cannot capture, matching the guarantee of a static lambda. Lambdas are anonymous and always become delegates when stored or passed to APIs that expect Func or Action.

entries.plainDefinition: A named method nested inside another method, property getter, or similar member.
entries.example: IEnumerable<int> Evens() { for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) if (i % 2 == 0) yield return i; }

entries.plainDefinition: Pauses an iterator method and returns the next value. Lambdas cannot contain yield.
Compiler-generated type holding captured variables. Local functions avoid this when called directly without converting to a delegate.
entries.example: Calling Pages() directly may skip heap allocation that a Func would require.

blocks.text: Choose local functions when you need **yield return**, recursion without dummy assignments, attributes on the helper, or argument validation before an iterator runs. A SkiaSharp render helper that yields tiles should validate pageCount in the outer method, then return an iterator from a local function — otherwise the exception appears only on the first MoveNext. Choose lambdas when the API demands a delegate: LINQ, Task.Run, events.

blocks.title: The iterator validation pattern
blocks.body: Put ArgumentNullException and range checks in the outer method. Put yield return in the local function. The caller gets immediate errors and proper IDisposable cleanup when enumeration ends.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Does the API require a delegate?
items.body: LINQ, Task.Run, and events need Func/Action — use a lambda (or method group).

items.title: Do you need yield or recursion?
items.body: Local functions support yield return and can call themselves by name without a forward declaration.

items.title: Will you call it directly?
items.body: Direct calls to a local function may avoid delegate and closure allocation. Converting to Func in a loop loses that win.

items.title: Need static no-capture?
items.body: Both static local functions and static lambdas forbid capture. Pick syntax by whether you need a name and yield.

blocks.title: yield return in the validating method
blocks.body: If the outer method is the iterator, bad arguments throw only when the caller first MoveNext. Split validation (outer) from iteration (local function).

blocks.title: Local function inside an expression-bodied member
blocks.body: Local functions cannot be declared inside expression-bodied properties or methods. Use a block body for the containing member.

interviewTakeaways: Local functions: named, attributes, yield, recursion, optional delegate conversion.
Put argument validation in the outer method; put yield/async state machine in the local function.
static local function = no capture, same idea as static lambda.
Lambdas win at APIs that demand a delegate type.
commonPitfalls: Writing yield return in the same method that validates arguments, so exceptions appear late.
Converting a local function to a delegate in a loop and losing the allocation win.
Declaring a local function inside an expression-bodied property — illegal.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript nested function foo() {} is hoisted in its scope and can recurse by name. C# local functions are also in scope throughout the containing member, unlike const fn = () => that is temporal-dead before initialization.
